newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index steady on illiquid market.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index steady on illiquid market.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mixed in quiet trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, with the SAX index slightly higher on gains to shares of oil refinery Slovnaft.
Slovnaft closed up 10 crowns at 1,020, while steel maker VSZ, the most liquid blue chip on the day, was unchanged at 750 crowns.
Brokers said that apart from these two issues the market remained desperately illiquid.
"We see no enthusiasm and therefore no volumes on the market," Peter Lachkovic of Slovenska Sporitelna said, adding that he did not expect the situation to reverse in the near future.
Although some traders had expected VSZ to rise higher than 750 after the company announced it would double its dividend for 1996 to 40 crowns, Lachkovic said its current level seemed stable.
"I think 750 has been exactly the price (for VSZ) that makes both stockholders and investors happy," he said.
Overall volume increased to 132,618 shares, from 92,416 shares traded on Tuesday, while turnover eased to 33.91 million crowns, from 54.63 million.
